# TOMBO — full reference

Generated from current repository Markdown. Do not edit directly.
Main-branch reference; match an existing application's pinned release before use.

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/ai.md -->

# Using TOMBO with AI agents

TOMBO is a vendored, framework-independent CSS design system, not an npm UI
package. Start with this guide, then read only the reference needed for the task.
The repository's `llms.txt` is a small index; `llms-full.txt` combines the current
reference for clients that cannot follow links. Automatic discovery depends on
the agent: explicitly provide the file or URL when necessary.

## Source and version

- `tombo.css` is authoritative for tokens, selectors and current behavior.
- The top-level `docs/*.md` references and `examples/components.html` describe
  supported usage. `docs/superpowers/` contains historical decisions, not the
  current API contract; do not implement a historical proposal without checking
  the current stylesheet.
- Main-branch documentation can contain unreleased changes. When working on an
  existing application, inspect its vendored CSS/JS banner and recorded hash,
  and use the matching release tag. Do not silently upgrade a consuming app.
- Copy CSS and LICENSE from the same release as described in [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/README.md).
  Copy `tombo.js` only when theme persistence or copy buttons are needed.
  Do not invent an npm install command, CDN URL, React import or build step.

For an existing integration, read the [upgrade guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/upgrading.md) before
replacing vendored files or removing consumer overrides.

## Choose a reference by task

| Task | Read | Working example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Colors, typography, themes | [Foundations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/foundations.md) | [Catalog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/examples/components.html) |
| Containers, spacing, responsive content | [Layout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/layout.md) | [Docs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/examples/docs.html) |
| Brand marks and visual intensity | [Signatures](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/signatures.md) | [Landing page](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/examples/lp.html) |
| Inputs and validation | [Forms](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/forms.md) | [Catalog forms](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/examples/components.html#c17) |
| Application header and navigation | [Topbar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/topbar.md) | [App](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/examples/app.html) |
| Charts and data alternatives | [Charts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/charts.md) | [Catalog charts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/examples/components.html#c19) |
| Theme control and clipboard | [Behavior](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/tombo-js.md) | [Catalog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/examples/components.html) |
| Printing | [Print](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/print.md) | [Docs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/examples/docs.html) |

For complete compositions, start with [integration recipes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/recipes.md): a settings
form with an error-state replacement and a keyboard-scrollable data table.

## Implementation contract

Reuse the documented HTML and class names before writing custom CSS. Inspect
`tombo.css` for any class or token not shown in a reference; never infer that a
utility exists from its name. Use consumer styles for page layout and keep
vendored files intact.

- Keep body text in the body voice and instrument labels/numbers in mono.
  Use the display voice for Latin display headings, not Japanese headings.
- Shu is the current-position line, not a filled primary button. Use the existing
  green primary button. Preserve the docs/app/LP intensity choices in the examples.
- Reuse space and type tokens. Use `padding-block` rather than a padding shorthand
  on `.tombo-shell`, so consumer styles do not erase its horizontal gutters.
- Give each page a descriptive `h1` and a `main` for its primary content.
  Nest section headings by meaning, not by desired font size; keep navigation
  and the site footer outside the main content when they are shared page chrome.
  Use the [skip link pattern](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/layout.md#skip-repeated-navigation) before repeated
  navigation so keyboard users can reach main content directly.
- Use native links for navigation and buttons for actions. `aria-current="page"`
  marks a current navigation link; a tab widget needs its own keyboard behavior
  and `aria-selected`. CSS does not implement that behavior.
- Wire labels, required fields, help and errors as shown in the forms reference.
  Give scrollable tables a focusable, named region; give code `pre` elements
  `tabindex="0"`. Do not remove focus outlines.
- Avoid assuming every foreground works on every surface. Read the supported
  contrast combinations, especially on raised and glowing backgrounds.
- Keep optional JavaScript optional: the page must remain usable without it.

## Verify the result

For a consuming app, run that app's checks and open its real pages. Check narrow
and wide screens, both themes, keyboard focus, overflow, and relevant error states.
Do not treat TOMBO's token contrast gate as certification of a composed page.
For this repository, run `npm ci` and `npm run check`; inspect changed components
in the local examples. Report any browser or assistive-technology checks not run.

Example request to an agent:

> Read docs/ai.md and docs/forms.md from the same TOMBO revision as our vendored
> stylesheet. Build the settings form using native controls and existing tokens.
> Preserve the vendored files. Verify labels, errors, keyboard focus and both themes.

## Maintaining agent documentation

Edit the source Markdown, then run `python3 scripts/build_agent_docs.py`.
Commit the updated `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`. CI runs the generator with
`--check` and rejects stale output, missing indexed sources, or broken local Markdown
link targets in the exported reference. External URLs and fragment IDs are not
validated; the local check also accepts existing directories. The full export
includes only the current reference, not design history or executable source.
No model API, MCP server, or extra package is required.

The generated files use main-branch source URLs; they describe the checkout used
to generate them and are not a versioned release service. For a release, fetch
these files and the references from that tag instead.

## Design rationale and research (2026-11-01)

- [shadcn/ui's actual index](https://ui.shadcn.com/llms.txt) groups links by task.
  TOMBO adopts selective retrieval so agents need not load the entire history.
- [Astro's AI guide](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/build-with-ai/) provides
  both index and full documentation. TOMBO adopts both access patterns while
  generating them from existing Markdown to avoid a separate, drifting manual.
- [The llms.txt proposal](https://llmstxt.org/) describes a concise Markdown entry
  point with links. It is a documentation convention, not a guarantee that every
  agent discovers or follows it. TOMBO also links the entry point from its README.
- TOMBO-specific choice: retain CSS and native HTML as the API. A tool server or
  framework-specific registry would add maintenance without being necessary to
  retrieve this small static reference. This decision can be revisited if actual
  integrations require executable discovery or installation tools.

# Upgrading a vendored TOMBO copy

TOMBO is copied into consuming projects; merging a change here does not update
those copies. Keep the source revision and SHA-256 hashes next to the vendored
CSS, optional JS, and license. The banner alone is not a content identity:
unreleased main-branch changes can still carry the previous release's version.

## Unreleased changes since v0.14.1

This section describes the current development line, not a published release.
Do not change a consumer's pin to a tag until that tag exists. Review the source
diff as well as this guide when selecting an update.

| Area | Changed behavior | Check in the consuming app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UI typography | Buttons, navigation tabs, TOC and tables explicitly use a 24px line-height. | Check wrapping, control heights and table row density, including column labels that now inherit 24px. |
| Metric units | `.tombo-metric > .v small` uses the shared 12px/18px note pair in all volumes. | Remove copied app/LP unit-size overrides and inspect units beside values. |
| Navigation | Empty or `false` aria-current no longer shows a current-position marker. | Use `page`, `step`, or another appropriate current value only on the current item. Remove empty-attribute workarounds. |
| Row headers | `th[scope="row"]` preserves letter case and uses table text size and data-row borders. | Check row height and identifiers; inspect consumer overrides before removing them. Column headings retain their existing style. |
| Code focus | Code controls use code-green for focus; the pre outline is inset to avoid clipping. | Tab to Copy and pre, check both themes, then scroll the code with arrow keys. |
| Compact controls | Theme and copy controls have a minimum 24×24 CSS pixel target. | Check caption height, alignment and narrow layouts with customized labels. |
| Status chips | Decorative dots retain a visible border in forced-colors mode and use the user's palette. | Keep an explicit status label; dot color alone must not convey the state. Check with your high-contrast settings. |
| Theme state | `getTheme()` reports this page's active selection even when storage fails. Invalid setting names are ignored. | Call `Tombo.setTheme()` instead of writing storage directly. Out-of-band storage writes are not a synchronization API; reload to read persisted changes. |
| Copy failure | A rejected/unavailable clipboard call selects the code and focuses pre before announcing manual-copy instructions. | Check the fallback with your syntax highlighter and focus handling. Keep pre focusable. |
| Skip link | New optional `.tombo-skip-link` pattern. | Adoption requires a first link and matching focusable main target; copying the CSS alone does not add it. See [layout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/layout.md#skip-repeated-navigation). |

No existing class or token is removed by these changes. There are visible and
behavioral differences, so this is not a promise of pixel-identical rendering.
The example-page heading/landmark improvements and AI documentation do not alter
markup in consuming applications automatically.

## Consumer update procedure

1. Record the current tag or commit, hashes, and any local edits. Compare local
   edits before replacing files; keep product-specific overrides in consumer CSS.
2. Choose an existing release tag and read the references from that same tag.
   The main-branch `llms.txt` links point to main and can describe newer behavior.
3. In a reviewable application branch, copy CSS and LICENSE from the selected
   tag using the [vendoring instructions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/README.md#quick-start). If the app
   uses `tombo.js`, update that copy from the same tag. Do not add JS to an app
   that does not need its optional behaviors.
4. Compute fresh SHA-256 hashes from the copied bytes and update the app's pins.
   Verify its CI checks those hashes. Do not reuse hashes from a different tag
   or from this repository's working tree.
5. Run the application's checks and review the actual affected pages, using the
   table above. At minimum check narrow and wide layouts, both themes, keyboard
   focus and relevant error states. TOMBO's own gate does not test application
   overrides or runtime data.
6. Review the application diff before deployment. Preserve the previous files
   and pin record in version control so they can be restored together.

For rollback, revert the application's vendored files, license, hash/version pin
record and any coupled markup or override changes as one reviewed change. Run
the same application checks again. Reverting only the pin text does not restore
an older stylesheet, and reverting TOMBO's upstream main does not update an app.

## Maintainer release preparation

A release requires a coordinated version change and tag; a documentation PR is
not a release. Keep current Quick start commands pointing to the existing tag
until the release is ready to be made available.

- Review the CSS/JS diff against the last release and the consumer-facing changes
  above. Additions such as the skip-link class should be reflected in the chosen
  release version and release notes.
- Update both file banners and all three vendoring examples in README.md,
  index.html and ja/index.html together. Update the site's visible REV labels.
  `package.json` is private tooling, not an npm distribution version.
- Refresh introduction-page measurements with `python3 scripts/check_size.py --write`
  after changing the file banners. Regenerate agent docs with
  `python3 scripts/build_agent_docs.py`, then run
  `npm run check`. Confirm the tag name with the banner check before tagging,
  for example by setting `GITHUB_REF=refs/tags/vX.Y.Z` to the chosen actual version
  when invoking `python3 scripts/check_banner.py`.
- Review and approve publication before creating/pushing the tag or a release.
  Do not leave public Quick start instructions pointing at a nonexistent tag.
- After publication, confirm the tag resolves to the intended commit and that
  tagged CSS/JS/license bytes match the reviewed artifacts. Verify the tag CI and
  published documentation. Only then propose updates to consuming applications.

The ordinary CI workflow verifies pushes/PRs/tags; it does not create a tag,
publish an npm package, or update consumers. Release publication and consumer
rollout are separate operations with their own review.

# Integration recipes

Copy a complete composition, then adapt its content and application behavior.
These recipes use existing TOMBO classes; they do not require a framework or
`tombo.js`. Load your pinned `tombo.css` before the consumer stylesheet. References:
[forms](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/forms.md), [layout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/layout.md), and [agent workflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/ai.md).

## Settings form

This is the initial, valid state. `/settings` is an example application endpoint:
replace it with your real handler and add your framework's CSRF protection before
using the form. TOMBO does not provide a backend or save settings.

```html
<main class="tombo-shell tombo-shell--reading tombo-flow">
  <h1>検証設定</h1>
  <p>プロジェクトの検証条件を設定します。* は必須項目です。</p>
  <form class="tombo-flow" method="post" action="/settings">
    <div class="tombo-field">
      <label for="settings-project">プロジェクト名<span class="tombo-req" aria-hidden="true">*</span></label>
      <input id="settings-project" name="project" type="text" required
             value="gesso" aria-describedby="settings-project-help">
      <p class="help" id="settings-project-help">一覧で識別しやすい名前を入力してください。</p>
    </div>
    <div class="tombo-field">
      <label for="settings-coverage">カバレッジ下限 (%)<span class="tombo-req" aria-hidden="true">*</span></label>
      <input id="settings-coverage" name="coverage" type="number"
             min="0" max="100" step="1" required value="90"
             aria-describedby="settings-coverage-help">
      <p class="help" id="settings-coverage-help">0から100の整数を入力してください。</p>
    </div>
    <fieldset class="tombo-fieldset">
      <legend>検証モード</legend>
      <label class="tombo-check"><input type="radio" name="mode" value="strict" checked>厳密</label>
      <label class="tombo-check"><input type="radio" name="mode" value="lenient">許容</label>
    </fieldset>
    <button class="tombo-btn tombo-btn--primary" type="submit">設定を保存</button>
  </form>
</main>
```

On server validation failure, preserve entered values and replace the affected
field with an error state. Keep help and error IDs distinct and point to both.
Use unique IDs if this composition appears more than once on a page.

```html
<div class="tombo-field">
  <label for="settings-coverage">カバレッジ下限 (%)<span class="tombo-req" aria-hidden="true">*</span></label>
  <input id="settings-coverage" name="coverage" type="number"
         min="0" max="100" step="1" required value="101" aria-invalid="true"
         aria-describedby="settings-coverage-help settings-coverage-error">
  <p class="help" id="settings-coverage-help">0から100の整数を入力してください。</p>
  <p class="error" id="settings-coverage-error">101は上限を超えています。100以下に変更してください。</p>
</div>
```

Replace the field; do not append a second copy with the same IDs. Once the error
is resolved, remove `aria-invalid`, the error paragraph and its ID from
`aria-describedby`. For dynamic validation, manage focus/announcements in the
application. TOMBO only styles the state and does not decide when it is resolved.

Check: labels focus their input; Tab reaches each control; arrow keys change the
radio option; native validation rejects missing names and out-of-range numbers.
Application tests must separately verify saving and server-side validation.

## Data table with local scrolling

Use a named, focusable wrapper so overflow belongs to the table, not the page.
Retain native table semantics and explicit column/row headers. The minimum table
width below is a consumer decision for these columns, not a new TOMBO token.
Place this CSS in the consuming application's stylesheet. TOMBO preserves
letter case in `th[scope="row"]`; column headers use the uppercase instrument voice.

```css
.endpoint-table { min-inline-size: 40rem; }
```

```html
<section class="tombo-shell tombo-flow" aria-labelledby="endpoints-title">
  <h2 id="endpoints-title">エンドポイントの検証状況</h2>
  <p id="endpoints-help">幅が足りない場合は表の枠内を横にスクロールできます。</p>
  <div class="tombo-table-wrap" role="region" tabindex="0"
       aria-labelledby="endpoints-title" aria-describedby="endpoints-help">
    <table class="tombo-table endpoint-table">
      <thead><tr>
        <th scope="col">エンドポイント</th>
        <th scope="col">ステータス</th>
        <th scope="col">検証結果</th>
      </tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><th scope="row"><code>GET /users/{id}</code></th>
          <td>200</td><td><span class="tombo-chip" data-status="ok">検証済み</span></td></tr>
        <tr><th scope="row"><code>POST /orders</code></th>
          <td>201</td><td><span class="tombo-chip" data-status="warn">未検証</span></td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
</section>
```

Check at 390px and desktop widths: only the wrapper scrolls horizontally; keyboard
users can focus it and scroll with arrow keys. Status remains understandable
without color because each chip has text. For zero rows, render an application
message explaining how to add data instead of leaving a blank table body.

For both recipes, verify light and dark themes and preserve the visible focus
indicator. Do not interpret a passing token contrast check as a complete
accessibility audit of the consuming application.

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/README.md -->

<p align="center">
  <picture>
    <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="assets/logo/tombo-mark-dark.svg">
    <img src="assets/logo/tombo-mark.svg" alt="TOMBO mark — a dragonfly drawn as a printer's registration mark" width="92">
  </picture>
</p>
<h1 align="center">
  <picture>
    <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="assets/logo/tombo-wordmark-dark.svg">
    <img src="assets/logo/tombo-wordmark.svg" alt="TOMBO" width="320">
  </picture>
</h1>

A single-file CSS design system for everything wadakatu ships — OSS docs sites, web apps, LPs, portfolios. Zero dependencies, one `<link>` — an optional `tombo.js` adds theme persistence and copy buttons, but no page needs it.

The goal is not a component library. It's recognition: the same handful of signature marks, repeated without exception across every product, at a "volume" tuned to context — quiet in docs, loud in an LP.

## Name

**トンボ (tombo)** is a printer's registration mark — the small cross drawn on a printing plate so every layer of ink aligns to the same point. It is the mark that measures.

It's also a homophone for **蜻蛉 (tombo)**, the dragonfly: an insect that only flies forward, never backward, which made it a symbol of victory (**勝ち虫**, *kachimushi*) to samurai. *Katu* (勝) — to win — hides inside *wadaKATU*.

The logo is a registration cross with two wing strokes and a tail tick in shu (朱, vermillion) — the same red the system uses everywhere else to mark "you are here."

The dark flavor is named **hotaru** (蛍, firefly): at night, the instruments glow.

## The three rules

1. **すべてを測る — measure everything.** Elements sit next to dimension lines, tick marks, and running numbers. The sense that something was measured before it was placed is what gives the page its air.
2. **銘は等幅 — inscriptions are monospace.** Numbers, labels, indices, and units are always set in mono. Body copy stays in a quiet sans; only the instrumentation gets to glow in mono.
3. **朱は現在地 — shu marks the current position.** Red is reserved for a 1–2px line that points at "here" — the current tab, the current TOC entry, the current ruler value. The moment it fills a shape, it stops being shu and becomes plain red.

## Quick start

TOMBO is distributed by vendoring — no npm package, no CDN link to go down or drift. Copy the files out of a release tag:

```bash
git -C /path/to/tombo show v0.14.1:tombo.css > public/styles/tombo.css
git -C /path/to/tombo show v0.14.1:LICENSE   > public/styles/tombo.LICENSE
git -C /path/to/tombo show v0.14.1:tombo.js  > public/scripts/tombo.js   # optional — see docs/tombo-js.md
```

Then link your copy, alongside the three voices:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/styles/tombo.css">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Instrument+Sans:wght@600;700&family=M+PLUS+2:wght@450;500;700&family=Martian+Mono:wdth,wght@75..112.5,400..600&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
```

No build step, no framework — it's a single stylesheet, so any templating layer works (Astro, Laravel Blade, Vue, plain HTML). The font `<link>`s are optional: `tombo.css` declares font stacks with system fallbacks (`system-ui`, `ui-monospace`), so the page degrades gracefully without them.

A vendored copy drifts silently, so pin it: record the tag and the file's sha256 in the consuming repo and check it in CI. Then a hand-edit or a stale copy fails the build instead of turning into a mystery months later.

`tombo.js` is optional and independent: theme persistence, the `.tombo-themes` control, and copy buttons — see [docs/tombo-js.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/tombo-js.md) for the two script tags and what each one does.

For existing copies, follow the [upgrade guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/upgrading.md) for behavior
changes, verification and rollback. Main may contain changes not yet in a release.

## AI-assisted integration

Start with [the agent guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/ai.md) for task-specific references and integration
constraints. [llms.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/llms.txt) is the concise index; [llms-full.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/llms-full.txt)
is the generated full reference. Match the documentation to your vendored release.

The design history — every spec and plan that shaped a release — is under [docs/superpowers/](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/superpowers/).

## Examples

Three volumes of the same language, side by side:

- `examples/docs.html` — documentation site
- `examples/app.html` — web application
- `examples/lp.html` — landing page
- `examples/components.html` — the component catalog: every component as a live demo + copy-paste markup, dogfooded at docs volume

Each toggles `tombo` / `hotaru` live and can be opened directly in a browser (no build step).

## Contrast gate

40 token pairs (light + dark, on paper, surface, and supported raised combinations) are checked against WCAG 2.1 floors — 7:1 for primary body text, 4.5:1 for secondary text and interactive color, 3:1 for non-text (lines, status dots). Token values are parsed from `tombo.css` itself, so editing a token there is automatically re-checked.

```bash
python3 scripts/check_contrast.py       # runs the gate, exits 1 on any violation
python3 scripts/check_contrast.py --self-test   # verifies the luminance math itself
```

## CI

Every push to `main`, every `v*` tag, and every pull request runs one gate —
the same `npm run check` you can run locally before merging:

1. **stylelint + [`use-baseline`](https://github.com/ryo-manba/stylelint-plugin-use-baseline)** (`available: "widely"`) — keeps `tombo.css` inside Baseline. Deliberately non-widely features (progressive enhancement) are listed, with justification, in `stylelint.config.mjs` — that list is the project's PE ledger.
2. **Contrast** — `scripts/check_contrast.py` (above).
3. **Size budget** — `scripts/check_size.py` (gzipped-byte ceilings and current measurements in both introduction pages).
4. **Banner / tag integrity** — `scripts/check_banner.py` asserts the version agrees across both banners and the three vendoring pins, and matches the tag on a release.
5. **JS syntax** — `node --check tombo.js`.

There's no build step and nothing is published; CI only verifies. Run the whole
gate yourself with `npm run check` (Node + Python 3 required for dev only).

After changing `tombo.css` or `tombo.js`, run
`python3 scripts/check_size.py --write` to refresh both introduction pages' byte
counts, decimal KB labels and budget ruler from the same gzip measurement.
Commit those updates with the asset change. The ordinary check is read-only and
fails on stale values or missing measurement markers; `--write` still fails if
an asset exceeds its budget. These measurements describe this checkout, while
Quick start pins continue to point to the published release.

### Visual regression

Run `npm run test:visual` (Docker required). A separate CI job uses the same
Playwright image and Linux/amd64 architecture to compare full-page screenshots
of every `examples/*.html` page in both themes at 1280×900. The regular
`npm run check` remains browser-free. On failure, CI uploads the HTML report,
expected/actual/diff images and traces as the `visual-diff` artifact.

For an intentional visual change, run `npm run test:visual:update`, review the
changed images in `tests/visual/snapshots/`, then commit them with the change.
Never update baselines just to make an unexplained failure pass. A missing
baseline fails the comparison; CI does not create or accept new baselines.

The test replaces Google Fonts responses with the same font families from
locked Fontsource development dependencies (including Martian Mono's width
axis), waits for fonts, and disables animations during capture. Other external
requests fail. This stabilizes comparisons without changing the shipped pages.
Playwright and font upgrades require a reviewed baseline update. The container
version follows the exact `@playwright/test` version in package.json.

These are desktop Chromium regressions, not a substitute for mobile layouts,
interaction, accessibility or other-browser checks. Rendering is environment
dependent; use the wrapper commands above rather than native screenshot runs.
See [Playwright visual comparisons](https://playwright.dev/docs/test-snapshots)
and [the official Docker environment](https://playwright.dev/docs/docker).

## Scope

Zero dependencies — one `tombo.css` file (`@layer tombo.reset, tombo.tokens, tombo.base, tombo.components, tombo.utilities`), plus an **optional** `tombo.js` for theme persistence and copy buttons (see [docs/tombo-js.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/tombo-js.md)). It's progressive enhancement, not a requirement: every page renders and works with `tombo.css` alone and no JS at all, following the OS theme; `tombo.js` only makes a chosen theme remember itself across visits and adds the copy buttons. Distributed by vendoring from a tag — there is no CDN and no npm package, deliberately.

Deliberately out of scope for v1: Figma kit, JS components, framework wrappers (React/Vue), an icon set beyond the logo, and **npm publishing** — these are follow-ups once the CSS itself is stable.

## License

MIT — see [LICENSE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/LICENSE).

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/foundations.md -->

# Foundations

The three voices, the two themes, and the token table everything else is built from.

## Type

Three voices, selected zero-base with the reader first (see `superpowers/specs/2026-07-21-tombo-typography-design.md`):

| Voice | Face | Role |
|---|---|---|
| DISPLAY | Instrument Sans 700 | Latin display headings only (tracking -.015em never touches Japanese) |
| BODY | M PLUS 2 at weight 450 | Japanese body, UI copy, Japanese headings |
| INSTRUMENT | Martian Mono | labels, numbers, indices, code (code condenses to width 87.5%) |

A 10-step type scale (`--tombo-text-*` / `--tombo-lh-*`, body 15px/30px) replaces all ad-hoc sizes — components may only reference scale tokens.

Use the size and line-height tokens as a pair. Buttons, navigation tabs, the
table of contents and data tables explicitly use the UI line-height (24px),
rather than inheriting body text's unitless line-height. Table column labels
keep their smaller label font size within that shared 24px line box.

Units inside `.tombo-metric > .v small` use the note pair (12px/18px), weight
400 and `--tombo-ink-faint` in every volume. Use the same markup in an app or
LP; no page-specific size override is needed:

```html
<div class="tombo-metric">
  <div class="k">COVERAGE</div>
  <div class="v">96.2<small>%</small></div>
</div>
```

## Themes

TOMBO ships two flavors, structured like catppuccin's: one umbrella system name, two `data-theme` values.

| Theme | Role |
|---|---|
| `tombo` | Day drawing (light, default) |
| `hotaru` | Night drawing (dark) |

By default the page follows the OS via `color-scheme: light dark` and `light-dark()` token values — no flag needed. To force a theme, set `data-theme` on `<html>`:

```html
<html data-theme="hotaru">
```

```js
document.documentElement.dataset.theme = "hotaru"; // or "tombo"
```

## Tokens

Prefix: `--tombo-`. Only the values change between themes; the token names don't.

### tombo (day)

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| paper | `#F2F4EF` | page background (greenish drafting paper) |
| surface | `#FAFBF8` | cards / panels (+1 step) |
| ink | `#1A211D` | body text, primary rules |
| ink-sub | `#4C5650` | secondary text |
| ink-faint | `#667069` | annotations, numbers |
| hairline | `rgba(26,33,29,.16)` | rules |
| grid | `rgba(26,33,29,.07)` | graph paper |
| green | `#0E5A47` | brand / interactive (links, buttons, ticks) |
| shu | `#D8442B` | current-position line only |

Day has no `raised` (+2) step — pure white is forbidden, so there's no headroom above the paper's own lightness. The +2 step is faked with `surface` + a 1.5px `ink` rule instead.

### hotaru (night)

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| paper | `#131714` | page background (greenish ink-black) |
| surface | `#1A201C` | +1 step |
| raised | `#212824` | +2 step |
| ink | `#E5EBE6` | body text (moonlight) |
| ink-sub | `#9AA69F` | secondary text |
| ink-faint | `#808D86` | annotations, numbers |
| hairline | `rgba(229,235,230,.14)` | rules |
| grid | `rgba(229,235,230,.05)` | graph paper (~half of day) |
| green | `#4FC2A2` | instrument glow — the fireflies |
| shu | `#E5654C` | current-position line only |

### Status (app volume only)

| State | Day | Night | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| success | `#2C7A4B` | `#57B98A` | distinct from brand green in saturation and role |
| warn | `#B07818` | `#D9A441` | |
| error | `#A6301C` (crimson) | `#D06A5A` | **fills are allowed** — distinguished from shu by weight and role: shu = position, crimson = failure |

Forbidden everywhere: pure `#000`/`#FFF`, filled shu, shu body text, and any shadow with an offset — a shadow that implies a light source. The one exception is the offset-zero glow of [`.tombo-glow`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/signatures.md#glow), which is opt-in and night-only.

## Japanese typography

Mixed Japanese/Latin (和欧混植) spacing is CSS-native — you don't hand-type spaces between the scripts. `tombo.css` opts into [`text-autospace: normal`](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-text-4/#text-autospace-property) on `body`, so the browser inserts the proper 八分アキ (1/8 em) at every Japanese↔Latin/number boundary. Verbatim text (`code`, `kbd`, `samp`, `pre`) is exempt.

```html
<!-- write it tight; the browser does the spacing -->
<p>Laravel 11以降に対応し、OpenAPIドキュメントを生成する。</p>
```

It's progressive enhancement: supporting engines (Chromium today) render the 八分アキ; others render tight — fully legible — and pick it up automatically as they ship `text-autospace`, with no change to your markup. A hand-typed space, if you leave one in, is respected and suppresses autospace at that boundary.

## Supported text on raised surfaces

Use `ink` for body text, `ink-sub` for secondary text, and `green` for links
on `raised`. These pairs are covered by `scripts/check_contrast.py` in both themes.
Do not assume every foreground token works on every surface: in hotaru,
`ink-faint` on `raised` measures 4.36:1 and `error` measures 4.23:1, below the
4.5:1 floor for normal text. Keep error text on `paper` or `surface`; use
`ink-sub` for annotations on `raised`. The current CSS does not itself use
`raised` as a component background.

The floor comes from [WCAG contrast minimum](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html).
These token checks do not certify a composed page: overlays, overrides and
interaction states still need browser verification.

---

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/layout.md -->

# Layout

Containers, the space scale, and vertical rhythm.

## Containers

One class, `.tombo-shell`, and a four-step scale. The step is chosen by what the container holds, not by screen size.

| Token | Value | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `--tombo-shell-reading` | `65ch` | body copy — caps the line at 621px at the body voice, 76 latin / 41 japanese characters |
| `--tombo-shell-default` | `1280px` | ordinary pages and documentation |
| `--tombo-shell-wide` | `1792px` | landing pages, card grids, dashboards |
| `--tombo-shell-gutter` | `clamp(20px, 3.25vw, 64px)` | the inline padding, fluid across the whole range |

`reading` is in `ch` because it *is* a measure — it has to track whatever type it wraps, so the same token is wider on a mono caption than on body copy. `default` and `wide` are structural, so they stay in `px` to match the px type scale: a `rem` container under a `px` type scale lengthens the line without enlarging the text.

```html
<div class="tombo-shell">                       <!-- the page's width (default) -->
<div class="tombo-shell tombo-shell--reading">  <!-- body copy -->
<div class="tombo-shell tombo-shell--wide">     <!-- LP, grids -->
<div class="tombo-shell tombo-shell--full">     <!-- backgrounds, decoration: no cap, no gutter -->
```

Markup is the whole API. `.tombo-shell` reads `--tombo-shell`; the modifiers rebind it for one element. `.tombo-gutters` reads the same variable and adds the shell's own gutter, so the margin grid meets the content edge rather than the shell's outer edge. There are no container breakpoints — `max-inline-size` plus the clamp()ed gutter cover every viewport continuously.

`reading` is the only step measured on the text rather than the box: the shell is `border-box`, so `.tombo-shell--reading` sizes itself to `65ch` **plus two gutters**, and the line inside lands on 65ch wherever the viewport affords it. Below that the shell fills the viewport and the line shrinks with it — every step is a ceiling, not a fixed width. `default` and `wide` are frame widths and mean exactly the number they state. Applying `--tombo-shell-reading` directly to a paragraph — which has no gutter — needs no compensation:

```css
.prose p { max-inline-size: var(--tombo-shell-reading); }
```

Two things to know:

- **Don't use the `padding` shorthand on a `.tombo-shell` element.** Your rule is unlayered and `.tombo-shell` lives in `@layer tombo.utilities`, so the shorthand wins and silently zeroes the gutter. Use `padding-block`.
- **Code blocks and tables are not prose.** Cap paragraphs at `--tombo-shell-reading`; let code and tables fill the column. A grid item holding a code block also needs `min-inline-size: 0`, or its longest line widens the track instead of scrolling.
- **Wrap any table that can outgrow its column** in `.tombo-table-wrap`. A data table is a reflow exception under [WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html), but the scroll belongs to the table, not the page. The three attributes are one set — a scroll container that cannot take focus is unreachable by keyboard, and `role="region"` needs a name:

  ```html
  <div class="tombo-table-wrap" role="region" aria-labelledby="cap" tabindex="0">
    <table class="tombo-table"> … </table>
  </div>
  <p class="tombo-dimlab" id="cap">動作要件</p>
  ```

## Overriding the page width

The page runs at `--tombo-shell-default`. When a whole page wants a different step — an LP, say — reassign `--tombo-shell` once in your own stylesheet:

```css
:root { --tombo-shell: var(--tombo-shell-wide); }
```

**`:root` and nowhere else.** Because `.tombo-gutters` sits on `<body>`, the margin grid will not follow an override made further down — set `--tombo-shell` on `<body>` and it looks like it works while the gutters silently stop meeting the content edge.

When only one container needs another step, use the modifier classes rather than reassigning anything.

The system's one sanctioned inline custom property is `--tombo-ruler-value`; `--tombo-shell` is not one. Keep it in a stylesheet.

## Migrating from `--tombo-shell-max` (removed in v0.7.0)

`--tombo-shell-max` resolved as an alias for `--tombo-shell` from 0.4 through 0.6 — but **its value changed** in 0.4, so a page that read it without migrating shifted:

| | 0.3 | 0.4 |
|---|---|---|
| below 1600px | 1100px | 1280px |
| 1600px and up | 1280px | 1280px |
| the 1600px step | yes | gone — the scale replaces it |

The alias is **removed as of v0.7.0**. A page still reading `var(--tombo-shell-max, 1100px)` now falls back to its own `1100px` default because the variable is undefined — it can look unchanged while silently diverging from the system, so migrate off it. To migrate, drop your hand-rolled container and pick the step by what it holds:

```css
/* 0.3 */
.site-shell { max-width: var(--tombo-shell-max, 1100px); margin: 0 auto; padding: 0 32px; }
```
```html
<!-- 0.4 — no CSS of your own -->
<div class="tombo-shell">                       <!-- was: the 1280px case -->
<div class="tombo-shell tombo-shell--reading">  <!-- was: the 1100px prose case -->
```

If a page was relying on 1100px specifically, that was a measure, and `--tombo-shell-reading` (65ch) is what it wanted — narrower, and it tracks the type instead of guessing at it.

## Space scale

Spacing is tokenised on a 4px base. Steps 24 and up are multiples of the 24px grid cell, so block and section rhythm sit on the same grid the margin marks draw.

| token | px | typical use |
|---|---|---|
| `--tombo-space-4` | 4 | hairline gap, eyebrow → title |
| `--tombo-space-8` | 8 | chip / row padding, tight caption |
| `--tombo-space-12` | 12 | button padding-y, tight rhythm |
| `--tombo-space-16` | 16 | callout / code inset, body rhythm, card gap |
| `--tombo-space-24` | 24 | one grid cell — default block rhythm |
| `--tombo-space-32` | 32 | medium gap between components |
| `--tombo-space-48` | 48 | 2 cells — sidebar gap, small section |
| `--tombo-space-72` | 72 | 3 cells — docs section rhythm |
| `--tombo-space-96` | 96 | 4 cells — LP section rhythm |

Use tokens for `gap` and `padding` in your own layout CSS: `gap: var(--tombo-space-48)`.

### Vertical rhythm — `.tombo-flow`

Add `.tombo-flow` to a container to space its direct children apart with a single grid cell. Override `--tombo-flow-space` on the container to change the default, or on any child to change the space that precedes it:

```css
.article { } /* markup: <div class="article tombo-flow"> */
.article { --tombo-flow-space: var(--tombo-space-16); }   /* body rhythm */
.article > h2 { --tombo-flow-space: var(--tombo-space-48); } /* more air before headings */
```

`.tombo-flow` uses `margin-block-start` on `* + *`, so the first child has no leading margin. Use it for stacked prose/content; keep `gap` for grid and flex layouts.

## Table row headers

Use `th[scope="col"]` for column headers and `th[scope="row"]` for row headers
in simple two-direction tables, following [WAI guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/tables/two-headers/).
TOMBO keeps column headings in the uppercase instrument voice with the heavier
baseline. Explicit row headings inherit the table's text size, font and color,
preserve letter case, and share data-cell padding and hairline borders. Wrap
technical identifiers in `code` when they need monospace. Markup supplies the
header relationships; CSS alone cannot make ordinary cells into headers.

## Skip repeated navigation

Place `.tombo-skip-link` before navigation as the first interactive element in the
body. It is hidden off-screen until focused, appears above the page using theme
colors, and is omitted from print. Keep it outside transformed or clipped wrappers.

```html
<body>
  <a class="tombo-skip-link" href="#main-content">Skip to main content</a>
  <!-- shared header / navigation -->
  <main id="main-content" tabindex="-1" class="tombo-shell">
    <h1>Page title</h1>
    <!-- page content -->
  </main>
</body>
```

The fragment target and `tabindex="-1"` move focus to the main content without
adding it to the regular Tab sequence. No JavaScript is required. Preserve the
focus outline on both the link and its target. Verify Tab → Enter → Tab: the
link appears, focus moves to main, then the next control is inside main rather
than back in navigation. See [WAI technique G1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/general/G1).

---

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/signatures.md -->

# Signatures (the 6 fingerprints)

Six marks repeated across every product, "played" at a different volume per context (docs quiet, app functional, LP loud). See `../examples/{docs,app,lp}.html`.

| ID | Name | Classes | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| S-01 | Registration corners | `.tombo-corners` (+ `.tombo-corner-tr`, `.tombo-corner-bl` for all 4) | 12px corner brackets on cards, figures, hero frames |
| S-02 | Dimension line | `.tombo-dim`, `.tombo-dimlab` | hr replacement — end rules + center tick + mono caption |
| S-03 | Tick marks | `.tombo-ticks`, `.tombo-ruler` | list bullets as green ticks; ruler = 10%-grid track + green fill + shu current-value line |
| S-04 | Running numbers | `.tombo-sections`, `.tombo-sec`, `.tombo-fig` | auto-numbered headings (`02 —`) and mono figure/note captions |
| S-05 | Shu current position | `.tombo-current`, `.tombo-kicker`, `[aria-current]` | the shu marker on active tabs, TOC entries, kickers |
| S-06 | Graph paper | `.tombo-vol-lp`, `.tombo-gutters`, `.tombo-glow` | background grid — full-bleed hero on LP, margins only on docs, off on app; the glow lights the grid at night |

## Volume dial

The same six marks, turned up or down per product type:

| Signature | DOCS | APP | LP |
|---|---|---|---|
| Graph paper | margins only | none | hero full-bleed |
| Registration corners | figures only | instrument cards only | hero frame + figures |
| Dimension line | hr replacement | none | under headings + captions |
| Running numbers | headings, notes | REV label | FIG. numbers |
| Shu current position | TOC, tabs | nav, instruments | first stroke of the kicker |
| Glow (hotaru) | none | none | hero + instruments, opt-in |

## Glow

`hotaru` means firefly: at night the instruments are supposed to glow. Until 0.5 that was one hard-coded exception on the LP logo tail. It is now an opt-in class.

```html
<header class="hero tombo-vol-lp tombo-glow tombo-corners"> … </header>
<figure class="tombo-metric tombo-glow"> … </figure>
```

`.tombo-glow` lights a surface, rings it, and haloes the display type and metric values inside it. Every glow token is `light-dark(transparent, …)`, so **the class is inert by day and needs no theme selector** — it follows the OS and `data-theme` alike through `color-scheme`. Writing the rules as `[data-theme="hotaru"]` instead would miss every page that merely follows a dark OS without forcing a theme.

Two constraints are baked in, and both exist because the mockups got them wrong first:

- **The wash is a background layer, never a pseudo-element.** `.tombo-corners`, `.tombo-dim`, `.tombo-ticks`, `.tombo-ruler`, `.tombo-current` and `.tombo-kicker` all own `::before`/`::after`. A glow built on a pseudo silently eats one of their marks the first time the classes are combined — in our case the hero's bottom-right registration mark vanished and survived two rounds of review.
- **Annotation ink is lifted one step inside the glow.** A lit surface sits ~1.3 contrast points brighter, which drops `--tombo-ink-faint` to 3.93:1 on the wash and 3.68:1 on a lit panel — under the 4.5 floor that `.tombo-dimlab`, `.tombo-fig` and `.tombo-footer` all depend on. `.tombo-glow` rebinds `--tombo-ink-faint`, so every component inside follows without being touched.

The contrast gate flattens the wash onto the background before measuring, so raising `--tombo-glow-wash` past `.23` fails the build instead of the review.

## Current navigation items

For `.tombo-tabs` and `.tombo-toc`, use `aria-current="page"` on the current
link. Omit the attribute or set `aria-current="false"` on other links; an
empty value is also inactive. Non-empty values other than `false` keep the
current-position mark, following [WAI-ARIA](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria/#aria-current).
Mark only one item in each navigation set as current. These are navigation
links, not a JavaScript tab widget (`role="tab"` uses `aria-selected` instead).

---

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/forms.md -->

# Forms

Native-first: TOMBO styles real `input` / `select` / `textarea` / `checkbox` / `radio` — no JS, no custom widgets. The look only applies inside `.tombo-field` (and `.tombo-check` / `.tombo-fieldset`), so it never hijacks an input elsewhere on the page.

A field is a hairline box with a heavier bottom rule that carries its state — the instrument's reading line: it lights **green** on focus and **crimson** on invalid. Labels use the mono instrument voice; the required marker is an ink `*` (shu stays reserved for current-position lines). Checkbox and radio use the native `accent-color`.

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `.tombo-field` | one field: label → control → help/error, stacked |
| `.tombo-req` | the required marker (`*`) inside a label |
| `.tombo-select` | wrapper that gives a `<select>` a themeable caret |
| `.tombo-check` | one checkbox/radio row (the `<label>` is the whole target) |
| `.tombo-fieldset` | a native `<fieldset>` reset, with a mono `<legend>` — for radio/checkbox groups |

```html
<div class="tombo-field">
  <label for="cov">COVERAGE THRESHOLD<span class="tombo-req" aria-hidden="true">*</span></label>
  <input id="cov" type="number" required
         aria-describedby="cov-help cov-err" aria-invalid="true">
  <p class="help"  id="cov-help">0–100の整数。</p>
  <p class="error" id="cov-err">0から100の数値を入力してください。</p>
</div>

<div class="tombo-field">
  <label for="fw">FRAMEWORK</label>
  <div class="tombo-select"><select id="fw"><option>Laravel</option></select></div>
</div>

<fieldset class="tombo-fieldset">
  <legend>MODE</legend>
  <label class="tombo-check"><input type="radio" name="m" checked> Strict</label>
  <label class="tombo-check"><input type="radio" name="m"> Lenient</label>
</fieldset>
```

The CSS styles the states; you own the accessible markup:

- Wire `label[for]` to `control[id]`; point `aria-describedby` at **both** the help and error ids (space-separated).
- Set `aria-invalid="true"` only when a field is in error; mark required with the native `required` attribute; show a "**\* required**" note once per form.
- Put radio/checkbox groups in `<fieldset><legend>`.
- States are pure CSS: `:focus` (baseline green) + the base `:focus-visible` ring, `:user-invalid` **and** `[aria-invalid="true"]` (baseline crimson), `:disabled` (dimmed), `:read-only` (recessed). `:user-invalid` shows validation only after the reader interacts; the `[aria-invalid]` hook covers scripted or server-side validation.

Controls are `width:100%`, so keep the form's container to a comfortable measure (a login form around `380px`, a settings form no wider than the reading measure) rather than the full page width. Deep styling of `range` / `color` / `file` / date pickers is deliberately left native.

---

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/topbar.md -->

# Topbar (トップバー)

Every app-volume page opens the same way: a full-width hairline rule, the brand in the display voice, mono metadata on the right shoulder. `.tombo-topbar` fixes that recipe so the first 20 lines of every product are the same markup — the brand is locked to `--tombo-text-body` (no more 14px/15px drift), the row aligns on baselines and wraps on narrow screens, and dropping `.tombo-tabs` inside needs no undo CSS (the bar absorbs `border-block-end: 0; flex: auto`).

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `.tombo-topbar` | the bar — full-width hairline bottom rule, `--tombo-space-16` block padding; put a `.tombo-shell` directly inside |
| `.brand` | the logo line — display voice, 700, `--tombo-text-body`, `-.015em`; a nested `<a>` inherits ink with no underline |
| `.meta` | the right shoulder — mono, label-size, ink-faint, `margin-inline-start: auto`; carries case (no uppercase transform) |
| `.tombo-topbar .tombo-tabs` | tabs drop in as-is — the bar removes their bottom rule and gives them the remaining width |

```html
<header class="tombo-topbar">
  <div class="tombo-shell">
    <span class="brand"><a href="/">SCREENBOOK</a></span>
    <nav class="tombo-tabs">
      <a href="/screens" aria-current="page">画面一覧</a>
      <a href="/deps">依存グラフ</a>
    </nav>
    <span class="meta">wadakatu@prod / REV 4.2.1</span>
  </div>
</header>
```

The rule spans the viewport because the border sits on the bar, not the shell — keep `.tombo-shell` as the direct child. Brand-only bars work too: `.meta` stays on the right shoulder via its auto margin. On narrow screens the row wraps; if a page wants `.meta` gone instead, hide it from that page's stylesheet — the component never does.

---

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/charts.md -->

# Charts (図版)

Charts are instruments too. `.tombo-plate` frames a figure — hairline border, `--tombo-space-24` padding, and overflow that scrolls **inside** the frame, never the page. Everything a bar chart needs is a class scoped under the plate, so the norms live in the vocabulary instead of each consuming page. The caption stays `.tombo-fig` (the existing S-04 mono 銘) on a `<figcaption>` above the frame.

| Class | Role |
|---|---|
| `.tombo-plate` | the figure frame; the SVG inside is fluid with `min-inline-size: var(--tombo-plate-min, 560px)` |
| `.axis` / `.base` | hairline gridlines / the single ink baseline — the only axis |
| `.bar` / `.bar.is-zero` | green single-series bars / hairline zero stubs (2px) |
| `.val` | the selective value label (ink, 600) — peaks only |
| `.now` | the shu current-position line — never a data series |
| `.tombo-tip` | the tooltip panel (surface, ink border, mono note voice) — your JS shows and positions it |
| `.tombo-numbers` | the `<details>` disclosure for the figure's data table |

```html
<figure>
  <figcaption class="tombo-fig">FIG. 01 — DAILY CONTRIBUTIONS</figcaption>
  <div class="tombo-plate">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 720 200" role="img" aria-label="日別コントリビューション数の棒グラフ">
      <line class="axis" … /><text …>12</text>
      <rect class="bar" … tabindex="0" aria-label="07/23 THU: 21" />
      <rect class="bar is-zero" … />
      <text class="val" …>21</text>
      <line class="now" … />
      <line class="base" … />
    </svg>
    <div class="tombo-tip" role="presentation"><b>07/23 THU — 21</b>COMMITS 14</div>
  </div>
  <details class="tombo-numbers">
    <summary>NUMBERS — 数表を開く</summary>
    <div class="tombo-table-wrap" role="region" aria-label="日次の数表" tabindex="0">
      <table class="tombo-table">…</table>
    </div>
  </details>
</figure>
```

The norms are part of the system: **one axis** (the ink baseline), hairline gridlines, **one green** for a single series (need a second series? split the figure — there is no categorical palette), **selective value labels** (peaks only; the full record belongs to the table), and **shu strictly for "you are here"** (the selected week, today — never a data color).

`text` inside a plate is automatically mono, label-size, ink-faint (銘は等幅). The `<details class="tombo-numbers">` table is the accessible data channel; the tooltip is a visual aid (`role="presentation"`, `pointer-events: none`) that your JS toggles (`display`) and places (`transform: translate(x, y)`) — no JS, no tooltip, and the figure still reads. Interactive bars get `tabindex="0"` + `aria-label`. When the frame can scroll but holds no focusable element, treat the plate like a wide table: `role="region"` + an accessible name + `tabindex="0"`, or a keyboard user cannot scroll it. Override the minimum width in your stylesheet, not inline:

```css
.trend .tombo-plate { --tombo-plate-min: 900px; } /* one wide figure */
```

---

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/tombo-js.md -->

# Behavior (tombo.js)

`tombo.js` is optional. It's a single dependency-free file that layers three behaviors onto the CSS: theme persistence across visits, wiring for the `.tombo-themes` control, and copy buttons on code blocks. Nothing in `tombo.css` requires it — every page renders and works with the stylesheet alone.

## Loading

Vendor `tombo.js` from a tag alongside `tombo.css`, with the same sha256-pin discipline — the pinned commands live in the README's [Quick start](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/README.md#quick-start).

Then wire two script tags around the page:

```html
<!-- in <head>, before paint: applies a stored theme with no flash -->
<script>try{var t=localStorage.getItem('tombo-theme');if(t==='tombo'||t==='hotaru')document.documentElement.dataset.theme=t}catch(e){}</script>
<!-- once, before </body> -->
<script src="/path/tombo.js" defer></script>
```

Both are optional, and independent of each other:

- **Neither** — the page still follows the OS theme (`color-scheme` handles that on its own); the `.tombo-themes` control stays hidden and code blocks get no copy button, since only `tombo.js` reveals and wires those.
- **The deferred `tombo.js`, no inline snippet** — a previously chosen `tombo`/`hotaru` theme still applies (`tombo.js` reads `localStorage` itself on load), and the theme control and copy buttons both work. But a reader who overrode their OS theme sees the OS-default theme paint first and then swap a moment later — a brief flash. A reader who never overrode it sees nothing, since the OS default and the stored choice already agree.
- **The inline snippet, no deferred script** — no flash, but nothing else: the `.tombo-themes` block never un-hides, no copy button appears, and `window.Tombo` doesn't exist.

## Theme control

You author the `.tombo-themes` markup; `tombo.js` reveals it and wires the clicks. Ship it `hidden`, since there's nothing to click when JS never runs:

```html
<div class="tombo-themes tombo-label" hidden>
  <button type="button" data-tombo-theme="system">system</button>
  <button type="button" data-tombo-theme="tombo">tombo</button>
  <button type="button" data-tombo-theme="hotaru">hotaru</button>
</div>
```

On load, `tombo.js` un-hides every `.tombo-themes[hidden]` block and sets `aria-pressed` on each button — `true` for whichever matches the current setting, `false` for the rest. Clicking any `[data-tombo-theme]` element calls `setTheme()` with its value: `tombo` and `hotaru` force that theme and persist it; `system` clears the stored choice and returns the page to following the OS.

Theme and copy buttons have a minimum 24 × 24 CSS pixel target without enlarging
their caption typography. Preserve this minimum when customizing their labels or
styles. Touch-heavy applications may choose larger targets in consumer styles;
24px is a floor, not a recommendation to shrink other controls. See
[WCAG target size guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html)
for the criterion and its spacing exceptions.

## `window.Tombo`

```js
window.Tombo.setTheme('system' | 'tombo' | 'hotaru');
window.Tombo.getTheme(); // 'system' | 'tombo' | 'hotaru' — the current page setting
```

Use these instead of touching `localStorage['tombo-theme']` or `data-theme` by hand — `setTheme()` updates the stored value, `<html data-theme>`, and every `[data-tombo-theme]` button's `aria-pressed` state together in one call; changing only one of those leaves the others stale until the next click.

If storage is unavailable or a write is rejected, the selected theme still applies
to this page: `getTheme()` and the pressed buttons reflect that selection.
Persistence across reloads is best-effort; a reload reads the saved setting again.
Invalid values passed to `setTheme()` are ignored.

## Copy buttons

Every `.tombo-code` figure gets a copy button injected into its `figcaption` automatically (one is created if the block doesn't already have one) — no markup required beyond the block itself:

```html
<figure class="tombo-code">
  <figcaption><span>SHELL — INSTALL</span></figcaption>
  <pre tabindex="0">$ composer require wadakatu/laravel-spectrum</pre>
</figure>
```

Opt a block out with `data-tombo-copy="off"`:

```html
<figure class="tombo-code" data-tombo-copy="off">
  <pre tabindex="0">…</pre>
</figure>
```

The button copies the `<pre>`'s text via the Clipboard API, reads "COPIED ✓" for 1.5s, and selects the code for manual copying, focuses the code block, and falls back to an `aria-live` announcement ("Press Ctrl or Cmd + C to copy") if the clipboard call is unavailable or is rejected.

Give every code `<pre>` inside `.tombo-code` a `tabindex="0"`, whether or not `tombo.js` is loaded — it's a horizontally-scrolling region, and one that can't take focus is unreachable by keyboard.

The code panel stays dark in both themes. Its focus indicators use
`--tombo-code-green`; the `pre` indicator is inset so the panel's clipped overflow
does not hide it. Keep the native outline enabled, including when adding syntax
highlighting or custom copy controls. These focus styles also work without JS.

## SSR (optional upgrade)

`localStorage` is the universal default, but a server-rendered consumer (Blade, Astro SSR) can go one step further: store the choice in a cookie instead of — or alongside — `localStorage`, read it on the server, and emit `data-theme` on `<html>` directly in the response HTML. That skips even the inline boot snippet, since there's nothing left to apply client-side before paint. `tombo.js` itself only ever reads `localStorage`; the cookie round-trip is something the consuming app implements on its own.

---

<!-- Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wadakatu/tombo/main/docs/print.md -->

# Print

TOMBO is named after the printer's registration mark, so it prints like one.

**Hardening is unconditional.** Any TOMBO page prints cleanly: a `hotaru` page prints on white paper (not a black rectangle), the dark code panel repaints to ink-on-white so it stays readable, the theme toggle and copy buttons disappear, glow and motion are dropped, and instrument blocks (`.tombo-metric`, `.tombo-callout`, `.tombo-code`, figures, table rows) don't split across a page break. The page margin is a consistent `16mm`.

**Real トンボ are opt-in.** Add `tombo-trim` to `<body>` and every printed sheet gets actual printer's marks in ink: a single 角トンボ (corner crop mark) at each of the four corners, and a センタートンボ (registration ring + crosshair) at each edge center.

```html
<body class="tombo-trim">
  <!-- your page — print it (⌘P) to see the トンボ -->
</body>
```

The marks are `--tombo-ink` — registration black, the all-plate alignment color — never shu (shu stays reserved for current-position lines). Browser print has no bleed area, so each corner gets a single crop mark at the printable-area corner — an honest homage rather than an imposition-accurate double mark with a fake bleed line.

---
